instructions: nfs-walker is a Rust libnfs-based filesystem scanner targeting ~180K files/sec sustained throughput. Reviews should prioritize: (1) libnfs FFI correctness — handle lifecycles, thread-safety of nfs_context, CString marshaling for non-UTF-8 paths, negative-errno semantics; (2) preserving hot-path throughput — LRU handle caching, READDIRPLUS batching, minimal per-entry allocation, batched SQLite transactions; (3) SQLite schema discipline — additive migrations only, WAL mode intentional, no per-row commits; (4) walk-loop error classification (terminal vs retriable vs per-entry) rather than catch-all early returns. Do NOT flag: `unsafe` blocks with clear SAFETY comments, `.unwrap()` inside `#[cfg(test)]`, or clippy lints that contradict intentional performance choices (e.g., `needless_collect` where the Vec is kept for cache locality). See docs/greptile-rules.md for longer-form guidance.

rules.rule: Every `*mut nfs_context` from `nfs_init_context()` must have a matching `nfs_destroy_context()`. Every `*mut nfsfh` from `nfs_open*` must have a matching `nfs_close()`. Prefer Drop impls or scope guards over manual cleanup in long functions. Flag handle acquisitions whose release path can be missed on early return or panic.

libnfs contexts are not thread-safe. The intended pattern is one `nfs_context` per worker thread. Flag any PR that introduces sharing of an `nfs_context` across threads, including via `Arc<Mutex<...>>` or similar — that pattern is wrong here, not a fix.

Paths passed to libnfs must be valid CStrings. Real NFS exports contain non-UTF-8 bytes and interior NUL bytes. Flag any `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` on `CString::new()` for path data — these must return an error rather than panic.

libnfs returns negative errno on failure; positive returns on read-style calls are byte counts. Error checks must use `< 0`, not `!= 0`. Flag any `!= 0` comparison on a libnfs return that can be a byte count.

The 180K files/sec hot path depends on: LRU file-handle caching, READDIRPLUS instead of READDIR+LOOKUP loops, batched SQLite inserts under one transaction, and minimal allocation per entry. Non-trivial changes to walker/nfs/db code must justify how throughput is preserved. Ask for `criterion` numbers if the change touches the per-entry path.

SQLite bulk inserts must batch under a single `BEGIN`/`COMMIT`. Flag per-row commits in the walker write path — they tank throughput. Prefer `INSERT OR REPLACE` or `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT` over SELECT-then-INSERT round trips.
WAL mode is intentional to allow concurrent readers during long scans. Flag any PR that changes the SQLite journal mode away from WAL.

Schema migrations must be additive. Never drop columns — in-flight or resumed scans must survive an upgrade. Flag `DROP COLUMN`, destructive `ALTER TABLE`, or any migration that removes existing fields.

Errors crossing the libnfs FFI boundary must be wrapped with `.context()` (or equivalent) describing what was attempted and against which path/handle. Bare `?` on FFI returns loses the operation context and makes failures unactionable in scan logs.

Walk-loop errors must be classified into terminal (abort scan), retriable (back off and continue), or per-entry (log and skip). Flag any catch-all `Err(_) => return` or early-exit `?` in the walk loop that conflates these — losing a single bad inode should not kill a multi-million-file scan.

New hot-path features should include a `criterion` benchmark in `benches/`. Flag PRs that add per-entry work to walker/nfs/parquet/rocksdb without an accompanying bench, or that regress throughput against the existing `walker_bench.rs` baseline.

Integration tests that require a real libnfs server must be gated behind a feature flag — they must not run by default in `cargo test`. Flag new tests in `tests/` that hard-depend on a reachable NFS export without a `#[cfg(feature = "...")]` guard.
